newsitem.title: BELARUS: U.S. tells new Belarus ambassador not to come yet.
newsitem.headline: U.S. tells new Belarus ambassador not to come yet.

text.p: The United States has told the new Belarussian ambassador not to come to Washington yet to take up his post because of Minsk's expulsion of a U.S. diplomat, a U.S. embassy spokeswoman said on Thursday.
Janet Demery told Russian Television in an interview that ambassador Valery Tsepkalo had been asked to stay at home.

"It was felt that his arrival in Washington was not appropriate at this time. This is in connection with the recent expulsion of the U.S. embassy first secretary," she said when asked if it was true Tsepkalo was not allowed into Washington.

The move followed the expulsion of a Belarussian diplomat from Washington, announced on Wednesday, in retaliation for a similar action against the U.S. first secretary in Minsk, Serzh Alexandrov, who is of Belarussian origin.
The first secretary and consul of Belarus, Vladimir Gramyka, was declared persona non grata and given 24 hours to leave the United States.
A Belarus foreign ministry spokesman said Tsepkalo had flown as far as Frankfurt but returned to Minsk "for consultations", making no mention of Washington telling him not to come.
The Russian news agency Interfax later quoted a Belarus foreign ministry statement as saying Minsk rejected Washington's action against Gramyka but hoped the affair would not sour mutual relations.
The agency quoted the ministry as saying Belarus could not "tolerate interference in its internal affairs".

But it added: "Under the circumstances, the Foreign Ministry considers it important to declare the firm commitment of the Belarusian leadership to a healthy development of long-term and all-embracing relations with the United States, without any complications."
Belarus arrested Alexandrov at a rally against hardline President Alexander Lukashenko on Sunday.
Minsk accused him of "provocative" actions at the protest, but Washington said Alexandrov was carrying out his normal diplomatic duties by observing a political demonstration.
U.S. ambassador Kenneth Yalovitz was also recalled for consultations to Washington this week after Alexandrov's arrest.
Yalovitz and his wife were filmed by Russian Television leaving the embassy with their luggage earlier on Thursday.
Washington has been a vociferous opponent of Lukashenko's increasingly authoritarian rule. Last week it cut off $40 million in aid because of Minsk's human rights record.
